subject: E2E tail-latency acceptance probe & schedule

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Stein <rachel.stein@novamed.com>, NovaMed Eng Team <ops@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Quick recap & proposed benchmark profile (p95/p99 acceptance)

Hi Rachel / NovaMed team —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick post-call recap and the concrete next steps we discussed so you can circulate to your SRE/infra leads:

Summary of ask
- Goal: validate end-to-end (client -> Redwood hosted API -> client) tail latency for your production workload and compare to your incumbent provider.
- Acceptance targets you mentioned as desirable: p95 around ~300ms and p99 no worse than ~900ms for typical conversational requests (we captured that as a user-experience target).

Redwood proposed measurement & traffic profile (attached as traffic-profile.json and the PDF):
- E2E definition: time from client socket write to final token received (includes TLS/TCP and our endpoint processing).
- Regions: run from your us-west-2 load generator to our hosted endpoint in us-west-2 to avoid cross-region noise.
- Token sizes: 70% short (<=64 tokens), 20% medium (200-400 tokens), 10% long (800-1024 tokens).
- Concurrency: ramp to sustained 120 req/s with 80 concurrent streaming connections for streamable responses; burst to 220 req/s for 2 minutes to probe buffer behavior.
- Measurement windows: 30 minute steady-state windows with 5 warmup minutes; collect p50/p95/p99 and distribution histograms.

What Redwood will provide
- Benchmark harness (curl/locust examples) and a prebuilt load profile file you can run from your infra.
- Token-level breakdowns and KV-cache hit metrics for the run.
- A/B comparison docs where we overlay your incumbent provider numbers vs Redwood.
- SLO acceptance checklist (slo-acceptance-checklist.xlsx) and the benchmark plan (redwood-p95p99-benchmark-plan.pdf).

Next steps (action items)
1) Confirm the benchmark window (proposing Oct 19 10:00 - 12:00 PDT).
2) Share the IPs you'll run from so we can whitelist and provision canary capacity.
3) We will send the load profile and a short script; please run a smoke test and send logs if you see large variance.

Attachments: redwood-p95p99-benchmark-plan.pdf, traffic-profile.json, slo-acceptance-checklist.xlsx

Thanks — happy to sync on any of the details.

Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Sergio — thanks for the recap and the attachments. A few clarifying questions from our SRE and infra side before we lock a window: 

1) E2E definition: when you say "client socket write to final token received," does that include our client-side JSON parsing/latency or strictly network + server processing? We want to ensure apples-to-apples against our current provider numbers (their metric currently includes client-side small overheads).

2) TLS termination: is TLS terminated at your hosted endpoint (we assume yes). Our incumbent terminates at the edge; please call out if your CDN/edge is in-path.

3) Streaming: for streaming responses we will use 80 concurrent streams during steady state. For the long prompts do you expect per-token throughput to differ significantly vs short prompts?

4) Measurement parity: could you share the exact locust/curl commands and the headers you expect (x-redwood-trace-id, any special headers)? We also need your list of IPs to whitelist.

If the above looks ok, Oct 19 10-12 PDT works for us. We also want to run a short baseline against our incumbent immediately prior to your run — do you have any constraints about run frequency?

I'll loop in Paul (SRE) who will own the load generation.

—Rachel
Rachel Stein

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Quick recap & proposed benchmark profile (p95/p99 acceptance)

Hi Rachel — quick technical clarifications from the infra/SE side (copied Ben for capacity approval):

- E2E definition: we will measure at the socket layer on the client load generator (request write timestamp T0) and final token arrival T_end. That intentionally includes network/TLS. We will not include your client JSON parsing time; please confirm you can capture T0 at just-before-send. This matches how your incumbent reported p95/p99.

- TLS/CDN: Redwood hosted endpoints terminate TLS at our regional edge. For hosted hosted-us-west-2 the TLS termination is in-region (no cross-region CDN hops). We'll detail the exact edge hostname in the runbook.

- Streaming behavior: per-token latency for streaming responses has two components: (1) token generation time in the model path and (2) network flush frequency. For long prompts (800-1024 tokens) you will see larger tail due to KV-cache eviction and backend batching thresholds. In our internal tests we saw p95 increase by ~20-30% for long prompts at high concurrency vs short prompts. We'll instrument and share token-level latencies so you can attribute where the tail arises.

- Load profile & headers: attached traffic-profile.json (already in Sergio's email). We'll provide curl examples and a locustfile with the proper headers (X-Redwood-Trace, X-Client-Region). Sample header set attached in the runbook.

- IPs to whitelist (provisional): 34.216.12.45, 34.216.12.46, 52.4.77.112. If you run from an ephemeral fleet, let us know and we can accept a short-lived range.

I also attached redwood-p95p99-benchmark-plan.pdf — it contains the exact metrics we will gather (p50/p90/p95/p99, percentile over token boundaries, throughput curves, error classification).

If Oct 19 10-12 PDT is confirmed we will provision canary capacity and an on-call engineer (me) will be present.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
